reviewMethod: Read the linked official licensing, workflow and FAQ pages. Direct source statements may become verified documentary claims. Editorial alternative/audience interpretations remain likely. These confidence labels describe evidence class, not hands-on product quality or human publication approval.

descriptions.2do: A task and project planner with a perpetual direct-purchase Mac edition; mobile applications and future updates have separate purchase terms.
descriptions.gimp: A free desktop image editor for photo retouching and composition, with workflow and interchange limits to check before replacing an existing tool.
descriptions.krita: A free digital painting application for illustration and related art workflows, with specific Photoshop interchange differences.
descriptions.paint-net: A Windows image editor with layers, adjustments and effects; the free Classic release and paid Store release use a proprietary license.

decisions.value: Krita 5.3 can load PSD text as editable text or as a paint layer after a prompt. Clipping uses inherit alpha; indexed-color image editing is not supported, although some indexed formats can be exported.
decisions.reason: Replace version-sensitive historical migration-guide claims with the current FAQ's concrete limitations. Do not claim PSD text is universally uneditable.
Painting fit remains provisional. Migration introduction cites old product versions and cannot prove all current differences.
Official Classic license and download page establish free use, distinct from paid Store distribution.
License defines free Classic and paid Store channels and prohibits modifying the application.

decisions.value: Current download requirements are Windows 11, Windows 10 21H2 or newer, or Windows Server 2022, plus specified 64-bit CPU/GPU requirements. The proprietary application license prohibits modification; additional formats may require plugins.
decisions.reason: Add documented platform and plugin scope instead of presenting only licensing restrictions as a user trade-off.
Layers and adjustments establish workflow overlap; full Photoshop replacement or built-in PSD support is not asserted.
